headline: Maple Street’s HOA Promotes Reporter Mid-Investigation, Halting Favor Fire in its Tracks
deck: Chickens strut back to their coops while goat ledgers wobble toward a twelve-block reckoning.
article:
The Maple Street Homeowners Association named local reporter Barnaby Fleece its new Senior Favor Reconciliation Coordinator, yanking him off the Favor Fire story that had exposed 47 shaky chicken-for-goat swaps. The promotion arrived the same morning those swaps threatened to ripple across twelve blocks.

Fleece’s draft on the vanished chicken was locked in the HOA vault as too delicate for daylight. Chairperson Margaret Billow declared the move necessary to keep the bartering grid from fracturing, though the announcement skipped any mention of the buried report.

Neighbors, including the owners of the returned bird, greeted the news with narrowed eyes; the promotion and the official containment notice landed on the same bulletin. Harold Tiller, still holding a borrowed goat, muttered that a few fowl entries hardly justified freezing the whole ledger.

The HOA now urges everyone to audit their own books and warns that a second watchdog may be posted if enough oats can be scraped together to pay for it.
author: Clara P. Ledger, Chief Barter Correspondent

oped.title: Hats Off to the HOA: Why Goat-Ledger Chaos Is the True Hero
oped.author: Reginald Q. Featherstone III, Supreme Arbiter of Unpaid Favors and Certified Chicken Psychic
oped.body: Maple Street’s HOA deserves a medal for elevating that meddlesome reporter to Senior Favor Reconciliation Coordinator and snuffing the Favor Fire before it devoured every last goat chit. Further digging only multiplies debts; I myself still owe three hens for a rake I never borrowed. The real villains remain those oversized hats that started the whole cascade. Mandatory hat registries and public brim-shaming would settle accounts faster than any investigation. My own ledgers are pristine, apart from three unprovable goat discrepancies. Progress requires fewer questions, not more.

stories.headline: Maple Street Chicken Returns Force Local Hatchery to Rebalance Entire Favor Chain
stories.deck: One restored poultry debt now requires three new goat entries before harvest season
stories.article:
The county extension office logged 47 new ledger adjustments yesterday after the HOA cleared the outstanding chicken exchange. Hatchery manager Linda Voss confirmed that every restored entry must now be offset against three separate goat obligations before any fall planting swaps can proceed.

Voss stated the adjustments will delay seed distribution by nine days unless residents submit sworn affidavits detailing exactly which neighbor currently holds the matching goat credit.

stories.headline: Suburban Man Charged With Unauthorized Ledger Alteration After HOA Promotion
stories.deck: Detectives recover 12 forged goat entries hidden in a backyard shed
stories.article:
Police arrested Thomas Reed, 48, of Maple Street after a routine favor audit revealed mismatched entries dating back to last spring. Reed allegedly adjusted his own goat balance to reflect services never performed, hoping the HOA distraction would prevent further review.

Investigators noted the forged entries matched the exact handwriting used on three neighborhood carpool schedules, confirming the pattern through cross-referenced signatures.
